prose: SemiAnalysis argues that consumer subscription plans are heavily subsidised yet matter far more than their revenue share suggests. They are about 10% of Anthropic's revenue but can take over 40% of inference compute, cutting blended revenue per megawatt by roughly $36M. A monthly payment buys credits, and each model and token type burns credits at ratios that differ sharply from API prices, so the value of a plan depends on those limits. The piece frames resets and limit changes as marketing and customer-acquisition tools, citing OpenAI's generous resets and Codex growth, and says modelling lab finances requires understanding them.
highlights: Subscriptions: about 10% of revenue, 40%+ of inference compute.
Roughly $36M lower blended revenue per MW.
Plans grant credits; credit ratios differ from API price ratios.
Basis: first part of a long article.
